context: A 2x2 small-multiples grid of parallel coordinates charts, one panel per region (North America, Europe, Asia, South America), showing 200 synthetic cars across 6 dimensions with cross-panel brush filtering.
first_impression: Structurally honest parallel coordinates with shared global scales enabling fair cross-region comparison.
what_works: Y-scales use d3.extent(cars, d => d[dim]) computed once from the full dataset and shared across all panels — this is the correct design for small-multiples comparison, preventing axes from jumping per panel. Canvas-based rendering sidesteps D3 key-function concerns entirely since visual elements are redrawn imperatively.
what_doesnt: No line.defined() guard exists, though it is moot here since synthetic data has no missing values. Brush pixel extents are shared globally via brushExtents using identical yPx scales per panel, which is correct, but there is no guard if panel sizes differ at runtime (e.g., non-uniform grid cells), which could silently mismap brush selections.
